Plan.title: Plan
Plan.description: Represents a subscription plan offered by the SaaS, defining features and limits for restaurants.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Plan entity.

priceMonthly.description: Monthly price of the plan in the default currency.

maxStaff.description: Maximum number of staff accounts allowed for this plan.

maxMenus.description: Maximum number of distinct menus a restaurant can create for this plan.

features.description: List of features included in the plan.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the plan was created.

Restaurant.title: Restaurant
Restaurant.description: Represents a restaurant or hotel establishment using the SaaS platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Restaurant entity.

name.description: Official name of the restaurant or hotel.

slug.description: Unique URL-friendly identifier for the restaurant, used in client-facing links (e.g., QR codes).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code where the restaurant is located.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code used by the restaurant.

planId.description: Reference to the subscription plan this restaurant is currently using. (Relationship: Plan 1:N Restaurant)

logoUrl.description: URL to the restaurant's logo image.

active.description: Indicates if the restaurant account is currently active.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the restaurant account was created.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account within the SaaS platform, associated with a specific restaurant or a super admin.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant this user belongs to. Null for super_admin. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N User)

role.description: The role of the user, determining their permissions within the system. Allowed values: super_admin, owner, manager, cashier, kitchen, server.

active.description: Indicates if the user account is currently active.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

Menu.title: Menu
Menu.description: Represents a digital menu offered by a restaurant.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Menu entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant that owns this menu. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N Menu)

name.description: Name of the menu (e.g., 'Main Menu', 'Breakfast Menu').

isActive.description: Indicates if this menu is currently active and visible to customers.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the menu was created.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a single item available for order on a menu, such as a dish or drink.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant this product belongs to. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N Product)

menuId.description: Reference to the menu this product is part of. (Relationship: Menu 1:N Product)

available.description: Indicates if the product is currently available for order.

variants.description: Optional list of variants for the product (e.g., 'small', 'medium', 'large' for a drink).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product was created.

Table.title: Table
Table.description: Represents a physical table in a restaurant where customers can be seated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Table entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant this table belongs to. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N Table)

number.description: Unique number or name identifying the table within the restaurant.

activeSessionId.description: Identifier for the currently active customer session at this table. Null if no active session.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the table record was created.

Room.title: Room
Room.description: Represents a room in a hotel where guests can order room service.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Room entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the hotel (treated as a restaurant) this room belongs to. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N Room)

number.description: Unique number or name identifying the room within the hotel.

activeSessionId.description: Identifier for the currently active customer session for room service in this room. Null if no active session.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the room record was created.

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents a customer's order for food and drinks.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant that received this order. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N Order)

tableId.description: Reference to the table if the order type is 'table'. Null for other types. (Relationship: Table 1:N Order)

roomId.description: Reference to the room if the order type is 'room'. Null for other types. (Relationship: Room 1:N Order)

customerPhone.description: Customer's phone number, used for loyalty program and communication.

customerName.description: Optional name of the customer for the order.

status.description: Current status of the order (pending, preparing, ready, served, delivered, cancelled).

paymentStatus.description: Current payment status of the order (unpaid, partial, paid).

totalAmount.description: Total amount of the order, including all items and any taxes/fees.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the order was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the order was last updated.

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents a single item within an order, with price snapshotting.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrderItem entity.

orderId.description: Reference to the order this item belongs to. (Relationship: Order 1:N OrderItem)

productId.description: Reference to the product from which this item was ordered. (Relationship: Product 1:N OrderItem)

nameSnapshot.description: Name of the product at the time of order (snapshot for historical accuracy).

priceSnapshot.description: Price of the product at the time of order (snapshot for historical accuracy).

subtotal.description: Subtotal for this specific order item (quantity * priceSnapshot).

InventoryItem.title: InventoryItem
InventoryItem.description: Represents a trackable item in the restaurant's inventory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the InventoryItem entity.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant this inventory item belongs to. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N InventoryItem)

name.description: Name of the inventory item (e.g., 'Tomatoes', 'Flour', 'Beef Steak').

quantity.description: Current stock quantity of the item.

threshold.description: Minimum stock level at which an alert should be triggered.

linkedProductIds.description: References to products that consume this inventory item. (Relationship: InventoryItem N:N Product)

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the inventory item was last updated.

CustomerLoyalty.title: CustomerLoyalty
CustomerLoyalty.description: Stores loyalty program data for a customer, uniquely identified by phone number within a restaurant.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CustomerLoyalty entity, typically a composite of restaurantId_phone.

restaurantId.description: Reference to the restaurant for which this loyalty data is recorded. (Relationship: Restaurant 1:N CustomerLoyalty)

phone.description: Customer's phone number, serving as the primary identifier for loyalty.

visits.description: Total number of visits or orders associated with this customer.

totalSpent.description: Total amount of money spent by this customer.

loyaltyPoints.description: Current loyalty points accumulated by the customer.

lastVisit.description: Timestamp of the customer's last recorded visit/order.

definition.description: Collection storing different subscription plans offered by the SaaS. Access is typically for super_admins or public read-only for subscription information. No 'restaurantId' needed as it's global.

Root collection for each restaurant or hotel establishment. Documents contain core restaurant details and are managed by super_admins, with specific restaurant staff having read/update access to their own restaurant's data.

Stores user profiles for both super_admins and restaurant staff. Each user document contains their 'restaurantId' (null for super_admins) and 'role' for authorization. Access is typically by the user themselves, super_admins, or restaurant owners/managers for staff within their restaurant.
Collection for digital menus. Each document includes 'restaurantId' for multi-tenancy. Managed by restaurant owners/managers, readable by clients via QR.
Subcollection for products belonging to a specific menu. Each document includes denormalized 'restaurantId' and 'menuId' for authorization independence and QAP compliance.

params.name: menuId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent menu.

params.name: productId
params.description: The unique identifier of the product.

definition.description: Collection for physical tables within a restaurant. Each document includes 'restaurantId'. Used for linking QR orders to a specific table.
Collection for rooms within a hotel (treated as a restaurant). Each document includes 'restaurantId'. Used for linking room service orders to a specific room.

Root collection for all customer orders. Each document includes 'restaurantId', 'tableId' (optional), and 'roomId' (optional). Anonymous clients can create new orders, while staff manage status and payment.

Subcollection for individual items within an order. Each document includes denormalized 'restaurantId' (implicitly required for multi-tenancy, though not explicitly in schema), 'orderId', 'productId', and price/name snapshots for data integrity.

params.name: orderId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent order.

params.name: itemId
params.description: The unique identifier of the order item.

definition.description: Collection for inventory items. Each document includes 'restaurantId' for multi-tenancy. Managed by restaurant owners/managers, with automatic decrement on order payment validation.

Collection for customer loyalty data. The document ID is a composite of 'restaurantId_phone' for unique identification within a restaurant. Each document includes 'restaurantId' and 'phone' fields. Managed by restaurant staff for loyalty program tracking.

params.name: customerUniqueId
params.description: The unique identifier for the customer loyalty record, formatted as 'restaurantId_phone'.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed for a multi-tenant SaaS application, prioritizing security, scalability, and debuggability according to the core design principles. The foundational element for multi-tenancy and authorization is the `restaurantId` field, which is explicitly included in almost every document that belongs to a specific restaurant. This adherence to a strict `restaurantId` per document is crucial for achieving authorization independence and enabling QAPs.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
1.  **`restaurantId` Denormalization:** For collections like `menus`, `tables`, `rooms`, `orders`, `inventory`, and `customers`, the `restaurantId` is a top-level field. Critically, for subcollections such as `menus/{menuId}/products/{productId}` and `orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}`, the `restaurantId` (along with `menuId` and `orderId` respectively) is denormalized directly into the child documents (`product` and `orderItem`). This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore security rules to ascertain the parent document's `restaurantId` for authorization. Consequently, operations involving these child documents are atomic and do not suffer from hierarchical authorization dependencies, simplifying rule logic and improving transaction reliability.
2.  **User Context in Token:** For authenticated staff users, their `restaurantId` and `role` are assumed to be present in `request.auth.token` (e.g., via Firebase Custom Claims updated from the `users/{userId}` document). This denormalizes the user's authorization context directly into the request, preventing repeated `get()` calls to the `users` collection within security rules. The `users/{userId}` collection remains the source of truth for these roles and `restaurantId`, aligning with the DBAC principle.
3.  **Anonymous Order Creation:** For anonymous clients placing orders via QR codes, the `restaurantId`, `tableId`, or `roomId` are provided in the `resource.data` of the new `order` document. While a `get()` operation is used within the security rules to validate that the provided `tableId`/`roomId` actually belongs to the specified `restaurantId` and exists, this is a data integrity check on a newly created root-level document, not a hierarchical authorization dependency for accessing existing data. This is an acceptable trade-off for anonymous write access while maintaining data integrity.

**QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters):**
1.  **`restaurantId` as Primary Filter:** The mandate to include `restaurantId` in every restaurant-specific document ensures that all `list` operations (queries) can and *must* include a `where("restaurantId", "==", currentRestaurantId)` clause. Firestore security rules will strictly enforce that `request.auth.token.restaurantId == resource.data.restaurantId` (for authenticated users) or specific validation for anonymous users, ensuring that a user can only ever retrieve data belonging to their assigned restaurant. This makes `list` operations inherently secure and QAP-compliant, as the database intrinsically filters by the authorization context, rather than relying on rules to filter results after a broad query.
2.  **Structural Segregation:** Collections are designed with homogeneous security postures. `plans` are global or `super_admin`-specific. `restaurants` can be accessed globally by `super_admin` but read-only by relevant restaurant staff. Other collections like `menus`, `orders`, `inventory`, `customers`, `tables`, and `rooms` are strictly `restaurantId`-scoped. This segregation prevents mixing data with different access requirements, simplifying and clarifying security rules for each collection.
3.  **Customer Loyalty by Composite ID:** The `customers/{restaurantId_phone}` path (with `restaurantId_phone` as the document ID) combined with an internal `restaurantId` field provides a robust, QAP-compliant way to query and manage customer loyalty data unique to each restaurant, optimizing for lookups by phone within a specific restaurant.

This structure facilitates simple, robust, and easily debuggable security rules by making authorization context explicit in every relevant document and leveraging Firebase's capabilities for efficient, secure multi-tenancy.
